newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian traders see LME copper charging higher.
newsitem.headline: Asian traders see LME copper charging higher.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices are expected to charge higher and test the next resistance level, while aluminium may struggle to continue its recent rally, traders in Asia said on Thursday.
"Copper might test the $2,580 to $2,590 (a tonne) level," said one trader. "But the upside is still heavy for aluminium."

Another trader added, "The backwardation in copper may widen further if the spot market gets tighter. We haven't seen much Japanese buying (of copper) and we don't feel any physical tightness in Asia."
Traders agreed copper was set to test the next resistance level after surging to $2,570, its highest since May 17, 1996, in a speculative rally in London on Wednesday.
At 0530 GMT, LME benchmark three-month copper was quoted at $2,560/64 a tonne, off slightly from $2,565/68 at 1800 GMT on Wednesday and little changed from Wednesday's afternoon kerb close at $2,561.
Traders were more cautious over aluminium, which was boosted by copper's gains and a 4,350-tonne drop in LME stocks in London overnight.
"The physical (aluminium) market is tight, but a potential rise in prices would be limited to about $20," said one trader.
"Prices are likely to fluctuate between $1,580 and $1,640 (a tonne) in the near term, particularly as demand is expected to decline during the summer," he said.
Three-month aluminium was quoted at $1,619/22 a tonne at 0530 GMT compared with $1,623/25 at 1800 GMT on Wednesday and $1,623 at the kerb close.
Traders said they were also carefully watching nickel for any effects from an ongoing strike at Inco Ltd's Sudbury operation. Inco is the world's second largest nickel producer.
They were also nervous about mounting problems at Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group, the world's largest nickel producer.
"You can't tell what's going to happen at Norilsk. It's like holding a bomb," one trader said.
He added that nickel might head for $7,500 per tonne in the near future. The metal finished at $7,260 in London overnight after peaking at $7,380. -- Nao Nakanishi, Tokyo Commodities +81-3-3432-6179
